question:
A 30-year-old female athlete presents for sports clearance evaluation. She is currently asymptomatic
but has a history of multiple spontaneous pneumothoraces. Physical examination reveals joint
hypermobility, a chest wall deformity with depression of the sternum (pectus excavatum), and a

decreased upper-to-lower body segment ratio. Which of the following additional clinical findings would
you most likely discover during her examination? Answer Choices: (A) Pes planus (flat feet) (B) Mitral
valve prolapse (C) Arachnodactyly (long, slender fingers) (D) Kyphosis (E) A midsystolic ejection
murmur heard best over the right second intercostal space (F) Increased arm span-to-height ratio (G)
Thoracolumbar scoliosis (H) Hyperopia (I) Aortic root dilation (J) Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis)
 A. Pes planus (flat feet)
B. Increased arm span-to-height ratio
C. Mitral valve prolapse
D. Lens dislocation (ectopia lentis)
E. Kyphosis
F. Hyperopia
G. A midsystolic ejection murmur heard best over the right second intercostal space
H. Aortic root dilation
I. Thoracolumbar scoliosis
J. Arachnodactyly (long, slender fingers)
